nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. Then the set $\{(x, t) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R} : \Lambda^*(x) \le t\}$ is convex.
nodes.title: The epigraph of the Legendre transform is convex

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. If $\Lambda^*(x)$ is a real number for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, then $\Lambda^*$, viewed as a function $\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, is convex on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: A finite Legendre transform is convex

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. For all $x, l \in \mathbb{R}^d$, we have $\langle l, x \rangle - \Lambda(l) \le \Lambda^*(x)$ in $[-\infty, \infty]$.
nodes.title: Fenchel–Young inequality for the Legendre transform

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda_1, \Lambda_2 : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$, with Legendre transforms $\Lambda_1^*$ and $\Lambda_2^*$. If $\Lambda_1(y) \le \Lambda_2(y)$ for every $y \in \mathbb{R}^d$, then $\Lambda_2^*(x) \le \Lambda_1^*(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: The Legendre transform is order-reversing

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$. For every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ of $\Lambda$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(x) = \sup_{l \in \mathbb{R}^d} \big(\langle l, x \rangle - \Lambda(l)\big)$.
nodes.title: Supremum formula for the Legendre transform

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be a function that never takes the value $-\infty$, with Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$. Then the Legendre transform $\Lambda^{**}$ of $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^{**}(x) \le \Lambda(x)$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: The double Legendre transform lies below the function

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $q : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be $q(y) = \|y\|^2 / 2$, where $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm. Its Legendre transform $q^*$ satisfies $q^*(x) = \|x\|^2 / 2$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$; in particular every value of $q^*$ is finite.
nodes.title: The half squared norm is its own Legendre transform

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be the zero function. Its Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(x) = +\infty$ for every nonzero $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: Legendre transform of the zero function away from the origin

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$ be the zero function. Its Legendre transform $\Lambda^*$ satisfies $\Lambda^*(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Legendre transform of the zero function at the origin

nodes.summary: Let $d \in \mathbb{N}$, give $\mathbb{R}^d$ its standard inner product, and let $\Lambda : \mathbb{R}^d \to [-\infty, \infty]$. The Legendre transform of $\Lambda$ at $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is the Fenchel conjugate of $\Lambda$ at the linear functional $y \mapsto \langle x, y \rangle$, that is, the extended real number $\Lambda^*(x) = \sup_{y \in \mathbb{R}^d} \big(\langle x, y \rangle - \Lambda(y)\big)$.
nodes.title: Legendre transform

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
